fullPassage:
Astronaut Yujin's Space Log

Day 1 Back to Space!
After blasting off from Earth, we took about 27 hours to reach the International Space Station, where we docked successfully. This is my third journey into space. After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest artificial space habitat in orbit 400 kilometers away from Earth!

Day 5 The World with No Gravity
Now I'm getting better at remembering where I am when I first wake up, but I'm still often confused about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain readjusting to an environment where height and weight lose their meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with one finger as if I were a superhero. Unfortunately, zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast. That's why I exercise for 150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.

Day 25 Starting the Day
The station orbits Earth once every 90 minutes, and the sun rises and sets every 45 minutes. However, our schedules are set to Greenwich Mean Time on Earth.

My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal space, which is about the size of a phone booth. Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There's no good way to spit in space because everything floats. Then, I look over the daily schedule sent by the flight control team on Earth. After a meeting with the Earth team at 7:30, I start work.

Every minute of an astronaut's day is planned by the Earth team. My work comprises lots of scientific experiments and maintenance of the station. My favorite experiment is growing basil from seeds as I film its growth every day. Having green plants in space is a delight!

Day 60 Spacewalk!
Today's mission required a spacewalk, one of the riskiest tasks on the ISS. We had to install the bases for some newly developed solar batteries on the outside of the station.

Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a room connected to the outside of the station, put on our spacesuits, and floated gently into space. The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead, looking like it was ready to come crashing down upon us. Forcing myself to focus on the task, I secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring just outside the airlock. We moved along the handrail to the edge of the station. The dark void in front of us seemed endless. Despite the safety cable, panic rose in me. I thought, "If my hand misses the handrail, I will fall into the void." The task seemed to take forever, but I finally managed to install the battery bases. When I turned my head, the bright blue Earth was still there. In the middle of darkness, its beauty was beyond description.

Day 99 One Day Left
I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is alarming and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically harsh things an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I'll miss lots of things here. I'll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk. I'll especially miss my basil plants, whose leaves have become a dense forest! All the same, I'll never forget how lucky we are to have that wonderful blue planet as our home.

Day 100 The Descent to Earth
Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees Celsius.

After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window, which was scorched black. We were falling faster than the speed of sound. Once we got into the atmosphere about eight kilometers above the planet, a parachute caught us with a sudden halt and dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky until we hit the ground.

It's hard to describe how heavy everything felt in those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt terribly heavy, and so did my legs. Getting used to gravity, which I missed in space, will take quite a long time. The important thing is I'm home. I can smell the grass and feel the wind and the rain! I'll remember how magical these things are for the rest of my life.

questions.passage:
After blasting off from Earth, we took about 27 hours to reach the International Space Station, where we docked successfully. This is my third journey into space. After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest artificial space habitat in orbit 400 kilometers away from Earth!

Now I'm getting better at ①<u>remembering</u> where I am when I first wake up, but I'm still often confused about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up ②<u>convincing</u> that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain readjusting to an environment where height and weight lose ③<u>their</u> meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each ④<u>were</u> a floor.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② convincing → convinced: 'wake up convinced'에서 주어(I)가 '확신하게 된' 상태이므로 과거분사 convinced가 필요. convincing은 '설득력 있는'이라는 능동 의미.
det.analysis:
✅ ① remembering: 전치사 at + 동명사(remembering) 구조 적절. 'get better at ~ing' 숙어.

❌ ② convincing → convinced: wake up + 형용사/분사 보어 구조. 주어 I가 '확신하게 된' 상태(수동/감정)이므로 과거분사 convinced 필요. convincing은 '설득력 있는/설득하는'(능동) ←정답

✅ ③ their: height and weight(복수 주어)의 소유격 their 적절

✅ ④ were: 'as if each were a floor' 가정법 과거. 직설법 was 대신 가정법 were 사용 적절
det.tip: 감정/상태 분사: 주어가 감정을 '느끼는' 대상이면 과거분사(-ed). convinced(확신한), confused(혼란스러운), excited(흥분한).

questions.passage:
My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal space, which is about the size of a phone booth. Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There's no good way to spit in space because everything ①<u>floats</u>. Then, I look over the daily schedule ②<u>sent</u> by the flight control team on Earth. After a meeting with the Earth team at 7:30, I start work.

Every minute of an astronaut's day is ③<u>planned</u> by the Earth team. My work comprises lots of scientific experiments and maintenance of the station. My favorite experiment is growing basil from seeds as I film its growth every day. ④<u>Have</u> green plants in space is a delight!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ Have → Having: 'Having green plants in space is a delight!'에서 동명사(Having)가 주어 역할. 동사원형 Have는 주어로 사용 불가.
det.analysis:
✅ ① floats: everything(단수 주어) + 현재형 동사 적절

✅ ② sent: 'the daily schedule sent by the flight control team' 과거분사 후치수식. 일정이 '보내진' 것(수동)

✅ ③ planned: 'is planned by the Earth team' 수동태 적절

❌ ④ Have → Having: 문장 주어 자리에 동사원형 불가. 동명사 Having이 주어 역할을 해야 함. 'Having green plants is a delight' ←정답
det.tip: 동명사(~ing)가 주어로 쓰이면 단수 취급. Having = 가지는 것.

questions.passage:
I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is ①<u>alarming</u> and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically harsh things an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I'll miss lots of things here. I'll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk. I'll especially miss my basil plants, ②<u>whose</u> leaves have become a dense forest! All the same, I'll never forget how lucky we are to have that wonderful blue planet as our home.

Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is resistant to objects ③<u>entering</u> from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the orbital debris that ④<u>will</u> otherwise rain down on it.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ will → would: 'the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it'에서 otherwise(그렇지 않으면)와 함께 쓰이는 가정법. will(단순미래)은 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ ① alarming: 'getting up into space is alarming' 현재분사가 보어 역할. 주어(getting up)가 '불안하게 만드는' 것이므로 능동 의미의 현재분사 적절
→ 본문: 원문 그대로 alarming. 감정 유발 형용사.

✅ ② whose: 'my basil plants, whose leaves have become a dense forest!' 소유격 관계대명사. 계속적 용법(콤마+whose)으로 basil plants의 잎을 설명
→ 본문: 원문 그대로 whose. 소유격 관계대명사의 계속적 용법.

✅ ③ entering: 'objects entering from space' 현재분사 후치수식. 물체들이 우주에서 '진입하는'(능동) 것이므로 현재분사 적절
→ 본문: 원문 그대로 entering. 능동 의미 현재분사.

❌ ④ will → would: 'the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it' — otherwise(그렇지 않으면)는 가정법과 함께 쓰인다. '대기가 보호하지 않았다면 쏟아졌을 것'이라는 반사실적 가정이므로 would 필요. will은 단순 미래로 가정법 맥락에 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: would otherwise = '그렇지 않으면 ~했을 것이다'. otherwise가 가정법 단서. will(단순미래) ≠ would(가정법).

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ sinks(가라앉다) → floats(떠다니다): 우주에서 침을 뱉을 수 없는 이유는 모든 것이 '가라앉기' 때문이 아니라 '떠다니기' 때문이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① confused(혼란스러운): 'still often confused about how my body is positioned' — 무중력에서 신체 위치에 대해 혼란스러운 상태. 원문 일치

✅ ② equally(동등하게): 'I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor' — 무중력에서 모든 벽을 바닥처럼 동등하게 사용 가능. 원문 일치

❌ ③ sinks(가라앉다) → floats(떠다니다): 무중력 환경에서는 물체가 가라앉지 않고 떠다닌다. 침을 뱉으면 공중에 떠다니므로(floats) 뱉을 방법이 없다 ←정답

✅ ④ work(일): '7:30 회의 후 일을 시작한다'는 문맥에 적절. 원문 일치
det.tip: floats(떠다니다) ↔ sinks(가라앉다). 무중력 = 중력 없음 → 모든 것이 떠다님.

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ faded(사라지다) → rose(올라오다): 안전 케이블이 있음에도 불구하고 공포가 '사라진' 것이 아니라 '올라온' 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① riskiest(가장 위험한): 'one of the riskiest tasks on the ISS' — 우주유영이 ISS에서 가장 위험한 임무 중 하나라는 맥락에 적절. 원문 일치

✅ ② gently(부드럽게): 'floated gently into space' — 무중력 상태에서 부드럽게 우주로 떠나간 묘사. 원문 일치

❌ ③ faded(사라지다) → rose(올라오다): 'Despite the safety cable'(안전 케이블에도 불구하고)이 역접 단서. 안전장비가 있는데도 공포가 '사라진' 것이 아니라 오히려 '올라온' 것이 자연스러움 ←정답

✅ ④ description(묘사): 'its beauty was beyond description' = 형언할 수 없는 아름다움. 원문 일치
det.tip: rose(올라오다, rise 과거형) ↔ faded(사라지다/희미해지다). Despite가 역접 단서 → 안전장비에도 불구하고 공포가 올라옴.

questions.passage:
After blasting off from Earth, we took about 27 hours to reach the International Space Station, where we docked successfully. This is my third journey into space. After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest artificial space habitat in orbit 400 kilometers away from Earth!

In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain readjusting to an environment where __________ lose their meaning.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 무중력 환경에서 의미를 잃는 것은 height and weight(높이와 무게)이다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① time and space(시간과 공간): 시간은 우주정거장에서도 GMT로 관리되어 의미를 잃지 않음
→ 본문: 'our schedules are set to Greenwich Mean Time'으로 시간은 유효

✅ ② height and weight(높이와 무게): 무중력 환경에서 '위아래' 구분이 없어지고(confused about position), 모든 것이 무게 0(zero weight)이므로 높이와 무게가 의미를 잃음 ←정답
→ 본문: 'Everything has zero weight' + 벽을 바닥처럼 사용 = 높이/무게 무의미

❌ ③ speed and direction(속도와 방향): 속도와 방향은 궤도 운동에서 여전히 중요

❌ ④ light and sound(빛과 소리): 빛과 소리의 의미 상실에 대한 언급 없음
det.tip: 무중력 = zero gravity. 높이(height)는 위아래 구분 불가, 무게(weight)는 0이 되므로 둘 다 의미를 잃는다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 핸드레일을 놓치면 fall into the void(허공으로 떨어질 것이다)라고 생각했다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① return to the station(정거장으로 돌아가다): 핸드레일을 놓치면 돌아갈 수 없으므로 공포 상황과 모순

❌ ② grab the safety cable(안전 케이블을 잡다): 핸드레일을 놓친 상황에서의 두려움을 표현하는 것이므로 안전 행동은 맥락 부적합

❌ ③ float back to the airlock(에어록으로 떠돌아가다): 앞문맥 'panic rose in me'와 모순. 공포의 원인이 아닌 안전한 결과

✅ ④ fall into the void(허공으로 떨어지다): 'The dark void seemed endless' + 'panic rose in me' → 끝없는 허공으로 떨어질 수 있다는 공포 ←정답
→ 본문: 원문 'I will fall into the void' 확인
det.tip: void = 허공/진공. fall into the void는 우주에서 떠다니며 돌아올 수 없게 되는 것을 의미.

questions.passage:
After blasting off from Earth, we took about 27 hours to reach the International Space Station, where we docked successfully. This is my third journey into space. After ten years, I'm back on this station, the largest artificial space habitat in orbit 400 kilometers away from Earth!

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 유진은 우주정거장까지 도달하는 데 약 72시간이 걸렸다.
이번이 유진의 첫 번째 우주 여행이다.
유진은 무중력 환경에서 자신이 거꾸로 있다고 느낄 때가 있다.

det.korean: ③ 'sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down' — 가끔 거꾸로 있다고 확신하며 깨어난다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 72시간: 원문은 'about 27 hours'이므로 72시간은 오류

❌ ② 첫 번째: 원문 'This is my third journey into space'로 세 번째

✅ ③ 거꾸로 느낌: 원문 'sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down' 정확히 일치 ←정답

❌ ④ 4,000km: 원문은 '400 kilometers'이므로 숫자 오류
det.tip: 내용 일치 문제는 숫자(27 vs 72, 400 vs 4000)와 서수(third vs first)를 주의 깊게 대조해야 한다.

questions.passage:
My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal space, which is about the size of a phone booth. Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There's no good way to spit in space because everything floats. Then, I look over the daily schedule sent by the flight control team on Earth. After a meeting with the Earth team at 7:30, I start work.

questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 우주비행사는 자신의 일정을 자유롭게 계획할 수 있다.
유진의 개인 공간은 전화 부스 정도의 크기이다.
유진은 바질 씨앗을 재배하며 성장 과정을 매일 촬영한다.
우주에서는 모든 것이 떠다니기 때문에 침을 뱉기 어렵다.

det.korean: ① 원문: 'Every minute of an astronaut's day is planned by the Earth team.' 지구 팀이 계획하므로 자유롭게 계획할 수 없다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 자유롭게 계획: 원문에서 'Every minute is planned by the Earth team'이라고 명시. 우주비행사가 자유롭게 계획하는 것이 아님 ←정답(불일치)

❌ ② 전화 부스 크기: 'about the size of a phone booth' 원문 일치

❌ ③ 바질 재배+촬영: 'growing basil from seeds as I film its growth every day' 원문 일치

❌ ④ 침 뱉기 어려움: 'no good way to spit in space because everything floats' 원문 일치
det.tip: is planned by = ~에 의해 계획된다(수동태). 주체가 Earth team이지 우주비행사 본인이 아니다.

questions.passage:
After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window, which was scorched black. We were falling faster than the speed of sound. Once we got into the atmosphere about eight kilometers above the planet, a parachute caught us with a sudden halt and dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky until we hit the ground.

It's hard to describe how heavy everything felt in those first few minutes after landing. My arms felt terribly heavy, and so did my legs.
questions.stem: 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 대기권 재진입 시 캡슐이 가열되어 불꽃 조각이 창문 옆으로 날아갔다.
캡슐은 소리의 속도보다 빠르게 떨어지고 있었다.
낙하산이 캡슐을 갑작스럽게 멈추게 한 후 하늘에서 격렬하게 흔들었다.
착륙 직후 유진의 팔은 가벼워져서 움직이기 편했다.

det.korean: ④ 원문: 'My arms felt terribly heavy' — 팔이 끔찍하게 무거웠지, 가벼웠던 것이 아니다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 불꽃 조각: 'orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window' 원문 일치

❌ ② 소리보다 빠르게: 'falling faster than the speed of sound' 원문 일치

❌ ③ 낙하산 급정지+흔들림: 'a parachute caught us with a sudden halt and dragged and swung our capsule wildly' 원문 일치

✅ ④ 팔 가벼움: 원문은 'terribly heavy(끔찍하게 무거운)'이므로 '가벼워서 편했다'는 정반대 ←정답(불일치)
det.tip: terribly = 끔찍하게/몹시(부사, 강조). terribly heavy = 정말로 무거운.

questions.passage: Now I'm getting better at remembering where I am when I first wake up, but I'm still often confused about how my body is positioned. In the dark and without gravity, my inner ear just takes a random guess as to my position, and sometimes I wake up convinced that I'm upside down. Of course, it's actually my brain readjusting to an environment where height and weight lose their meaning. I can use any wall equally as if each were a floor. Everything has zero weight. This enables me not only to fly but also to lift huge objects with one finger as if I were a superhero. Unfortunately, zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast. That's why I exercise for 150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the psychological stress astronauts face during missions
the physical effects of zero gravity on astronauts
the advanced training required for space exploration
the technological innovations of the space station

det.korean: ② 무중력이 우주비행사에게 미치는 신체적 영향(physical effects of zero gravity).
det.analysis:
❌ ① the psychological stress(심리적 스트레스): 심리적 내용보다 신체적 변화(위치 혼란, 초인적 힘, 근육/골밀도 감소)가 중심

✅ ② the physical effects of zero gravity(무중력의 신체적 영향): 방향 감각 혼란 + 벽=바닥 + 물체 들기 + 근육/골밀도 손실 + 운동 = 전부 신체적 영향 ←정답
→ 본문: 'confused about position', 'zero weight', 'lift huge objects', 'lose muscle and bone density'

❌ ③ advanced training(고급 훈련): 운동은 적응의 일환이지 훈련 프로그램 자체가 주제가 아님

❌ ④ technological innovations(기술 혁신): 기술에 대한 언급 없음
det.tip: 주제 = 글 전체를 관통하는 중심 소재. zero gravity(무중력)와 관련된 신체 변화가 반복 서술.

questions.passage:
Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees Celsius.

After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window, which was scorched black. We were falling faster than the speed of sound.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: the role of friction in generating renewable energy
the scientific principles behind atmospheric formation
the extreme dangers of reentry into Earth's atmosphere
the improvements in spacecraft heat shield technology

det.korean: ③ 대기권 재진입의 극심한 위험(the extreme dangers of reentry).
det.analysis:
❌ ① the role of friction in renewable energy(재생에너지에서 마찰의 역할): 마찰은 언급되나 재생에너지와 무관

❌ ② scientific principles of atmospheric formation(대기 형성의 과학 원리): 대기 형성 과정이 아니라 대기 재진입의 위험을 다룸

✅ ③ the extreme dangers of reentry(재진입의 극심한 위험): resistant atmosphere + 1650도 + friction + burn up + 불꽃 조각 + 음속 초과 = 모두 재진입의 위험 요소 ←정답
→ 본문: 'didn't welcome us back', 'temperatures up to 1650 degrees', 'falling faster than the speed of sound'

❌ ④ improvements in heat shield technology(방열판 기술 개선): 기술 개선에 대한 언급 없음. 위험 상황 묘사만 있음
det.tip: 주제 파악: 두 문단 모두 대기권 재진입의 극한 상황(마찰, 고온, 고속)을 묘사하고 있다.

questions.passage: I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is alarming and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically harsh things an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I'll miss lots of things here. I'll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk. I'll especially miss my basil plants, whose leaves have become <u>a dense forest</u>! All the same, I'll never forget how lucky we are to have that wonderful blue planet as our home.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 a dense forest가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 바질 잎이 무성하게 자라 숲처럼 빽빽해진 모습
우주 식물 실험이 예상보다 빨리 끝난 결과

det.korean: 밑줄 친 'a dense forest'는 바질 잎이 무성하게 자라 숲처럼 빽빽해진 모습을 비유적으로 표현한 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 바질 잎 무성 성장: 'my basil plants, whose leaves have become a dense forest' — basil plants의 leaves(잎)가 주어. '빽빽한 숲'은 잎이 풍성하게 자란 것의 은유. 유진이 가장 좋아하는 실험이 바질 재배였고, 100일간 성장하여 잎이 무성해진 것 ←정답
→ 본문: Day 25에서 'growing basil from seeds'로 시작한 실험이 Day 99에 'dense forest'가 됨

❌ ② 실제 숲: 우주정거장 내부에 실제 숲을 만들 수 없음. 비유적 표현

❌ ③ 열대우림 관찰: 'my basil plants, whose leaves'에서 바질 식물의 잎을 가리킴. 지구 관찰과 무관

❌ ④ 실험 종료: 실험이 빨리 끝난 것이 아니라 바질이 무성하게 자란 결과를 묘사
det.tip: a dense forest = '빽빽한 숲'이라는 은유(metaphor). 바질 잎이 풍성하게 자란 모습을 숲에 비유한 것.

questions.passage: Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. <u>This</u> protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees Celsius.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>This</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 우주에서 오는 물체(objects entering from space)

det.korean: 대기의 저항으로 인한 마찰(atmospheric friction)이 행성을 궤도 잔해로부터 보호한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 궤도 잔해(orbital debris): 보호받는 대상이 아닌 보호 '로부터'의 대상

❌ ② 우주 물체(objects entering from space): 대기가 저항하는 대상이지 보호하는 주체가 아님

❌ ③ 마찰열(heat from friction): 열은 마찰의 결과이지, This가 가리키는 보호 메커니즘 전체가 아님

✅ ④ 대기의 저항으로 인한 마찰(atmospheric friction): 앞 문장 'Earth's atmosphere is resistant' + 'create enough friction to burn up' 전체 과정을 This가 가리킴. 이것이 행성을 보호한다(protects the planet) ←정답
→ 본문: 대기 저항 → 마찰 → 타버림 → This(이 메커니즘)가 보호
det.tip: This = 앞 내용 전체를 가리키는 대명사. 대기의 마찰 현상 전체를 지칭한다.

questions.passage:
Unfortunately, zero gravity also makes astronauts lose muscle and bone density really fast. That's why I exercise for 150 minutes a day as my colleagues do.

The station orbits Earth once every 90 minutes, and the sun rises and sets every 45 minutes. However, our schedules are set to Greenwich Mean Time on Earth.

My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal space, which is about the size of a phone booth. Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There's no good way to spit in space because everything floats. Then, I look over the daily schedule sent by the flight control team on Earth. After a meeting with the Earth team at 7:30, I start work.

Every minute of an astronaut's day is planned by the Earth team. My work comprises lots of scientific experiments and maintenance of the station. My favorite experiment is growing basil from seeds as I film <u>its</u> growth every day.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>its</u>가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 바질(basil)의 성장을 매일 촬영한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 우주 정거장(the station): 정거장의 성장(growth)은 문맥상 부적절

✅ ② 바질(basil): 'growing basil from seeds as I film its growth' — its = basil의 소유격. 바질을 씨앗에서 키우며 그것의 성장을 촬영 ←정답
→ 본문: growing basil → film its(basil's) growth

❌ ③ 실험(experiment): 실험의 '성장'은 어색. basil이 직접 선행사

❌ ④ 지구 팀(the Earth team): 지구 팀의 성장과는 무관
det.tip: its = 앞에 나온 명사의 소유격. 'growing basil'이 직접 선행사이므로 its = basil's.

questions.passage:
Today's mission required a spacewalk, one of the riskiest tasks on the ISS. We had to install the bases for some newly developed solar batteries on the outside of the station.

Scott, my colleague, and I went to an airlock, a room connected to the outside of the station, put on our spacesuits, and floated gently into space. The large blue dome of Earth hovered overhead, looking like it was ready to come crashing down upon us. Forcing myself to focus on the task, I secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring just outside the airlock.
questions.stem:
Q: 위 글에서 유진이 우주유영 중 과업에 집중하기 위해 한 행동을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
A: I ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ to a ring just outside the airlock. (7단어) (영어로)
questions.wa: secured the hook of my safety cable
accept: secured the hook of my safety cable

det.korean: 유진은 안전 케이블의 고리를 고정했다: secured the hook of my safety cable.
det.analysis:
✅ secured the hook of my safety cable: 'I secured the hook of my safety cable to a ring just outside the airlock' 원문에서 확인.
→ 구문: secured(고정했다, secure의 과거형) + the hook(고리를) + of my safety cable(안전 케이블의). Forcing myself to focus on the task 후 한 구체적 행동.
det.tip: secure = 고정하다/확보하다. safety cable = 안전 케이블. 우주유영 시 반드시 안전 줄을 고정해야 한다.

questions.passage: I'll return to Earth tomorrow. If getting up into space is alarming and uncomfortable, coming back down is one of the most dangerous and physically harsh things an astronaut ever does. Back on Earth, I'll miss lots of things here. I'll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk. I'll especially miss my basil plants, whose leaves have become a dense forest! All the same, I'll never forget how lucky we are to have that wonderful blue planet as our home.
questions.stem:
Q: 위 글에서 유진이 지구에 돌아가면 그리워할 것 중 하나를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
A: the satisfaction of successfully ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ like a spacewalk. (7단어) (영어로)
questions.wa: finishing an experiment or a challenging task
accept: finishing an experiment or a challenging task

det.korean: 실험이나 도전적인 과업을 성공적으로 마치는 만족감: finishing an experiment or a challenging task.
det.analysis:
✅ finishing an experiment or a challenging task: 'I'll miss the satisfaction of successfully finishing an experiment or a challenging task like a spacewalk.' 원문에서 확인.
→ 구문: finishing(동명사, 전치사 of의 목적어) + an experiment(실험) + or(또는) + a challenging task(도전적인 과업). like a spacewalk은 예시로 빈칸 밖에 힌트로 제시.
det.tip: the satisfaction of ~ing = ~하는 만족감. 전치사 of + 동명사 구조. challenging = 도전적인.

questions.passage:
Mother Earth didn't exactly welcome us back with open arms. Earth's atmosphere is resistant to objects entering from space. Any object will create enough friction simply to burn up from the heat. This protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it. But it also meant we had to survive a fall through the atmosphere that created temperatures up to 1650 degrees Celsius.

After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity begin to return.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 대기의 마찰이 지구에 쏟아지지 않도록 보호하는 대상을 가리키는 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.

Q: This protects the planet from the ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ ___ on it.
A: (7단어) (영어로)
questions.wa: orbital debris that would otherwise rain down
accept: orbital debris that would otherwise rain down

det.korean: 대기는 orbital debris that would otherwise rain down(그렇지 않으면 쏟아졌을 궤도 잔해)으로부터 행성을 보호한다.
det.analysis:
✅ orbital debris that would otherwise rain down: 'This protects the planet from the orbital debris that would otherwise rain down on it.' 원문에서 확인.
→ 구문: orbital debris(궤도 잔해) + that(관계대명사) + would otherwise(그렇지 않으면 ~했을) + rain down(쏟아지다). otherwise + would = 가정법 표현. 대기 보호가 없었다면 잔해가 지구에 비처럼 쏟아졌을 것.
det.tip: orbital debris = 궤도 잔해(우주 쓰레기). would otherwise = 그렇지 않았다면 ~했을 것이다. rain down = 비처럼 쏟아지다.

questions.passage:
The station orbits Earth once every 90 minutes, and the sun rises and sets every 45 minutes. However, our schedules are set to Greenwich Mean Time on Earth.

My day starts around 6:00 a.m. in my personal space, which is about the size of a phone booth. Still in my sleeping bag, I click through new emails and brush my teeth. I swallow the toothpaste with a sip of water from a bag with a straw. There's no good way to spit in space because everything floats. Then, I look over the daily schedule __________ on Earth.

overlay.blank: sent by the flight control team

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오.

'지구의 비행 관제 팀이 보낸'

[조건] (1) by, control, flight, sent, team, the를 모두 사용
(2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것
(6단어) (영어로)
questions.wa: sent by the flight control team
accept: sent by the flight control team

det.korean: sent by the flight control team: 비행 관제 팀이 보낸
det.analysis:
✅ sent by the flight control team: 'the daily schedule sent by the flight control team on Earth' 원문에서 확인.
→ 구문: sent(과거분사) + by(~에 의해) + the flight control team(비행 관제 팀) = 수동태의 과거분사 수식. schedule(일정)이 '보내진' 것.
→ 단어 배열: [by, control, flight, sent, team, the] → sent by the flight control team
det.tip: 과거분사 후치수식: 명사 + p.p. + by 행위자. 'schedule sent by the team' = 팀이 보낸 일정.

questions.passage: After pushing our spaceship away from the station, we eased our way into the upper layers of the atmosphere to start our descent. We felt gravity begin to return. My watch felt a lot heavier on my wrist, and breathing got harder. The capsule heated up, and orange and purple flaming pieces flew by the window, which was scorched black. We were falling faster than the speed of sound. Once we got into the atmosphere about eight kilometers above the planet, a parachute caught us with a sudden halt and __________.

overlay.blank: dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 조건에 따라 영작하시오.

'캡슐을 격렬하게 끌고 흔들며 하늘을 가로질렀다'

[조건] (1) and, capsule, dragged, our, sky, swung, the, through, wildly를 모두 사용
(2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것
(9단어) (영어로)
questions.wa: dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky
accept: dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky

det.korean: dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky: 캡슐을 격렬하게 끌고 흔들며 하늘을 가로질렀다
det.analysis:
✅ dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky: 'a parachute caught us with a sudden halt and dragged and swung our capsule wildly through the sky' 원문에서 확인.
→ 구문: dragged(끌다, drag 과거형) + and + swung(흔들다, swing 과거형) + our capsule(목적어) + wildly(부사, 격렬하게) + through the sky(하늘을 가로질러)
→ 병렬 구조: dragged and swung이 parachute의 동작을 병렬로 서술
det.tip: dragged(끌다) and swung(흔들다): 낙하산이 캡슐에 가한 두 가지 동작. wildly = 격렬하게/사납게.

solves.reasoning: ① remembering: get better at + 동명사 OK. ② convincing: wake up convinced(확신하며 깨다)에서 주어가 확신을 '받는' 쪽이므로 과거분사 convinced 필요. convincing은 능동. 틀림. ③ their: height and weight 복수 → their OK. ④ were: as if + 가정법 과거 OK.
